<!--
TEMPLATE NOTES (delete in a real deck)

The deck tells a story. Someone wanted something, tried something, and found
out something; the method is what they found. Use people (who discovered it,
why they cared), history, or a recent application that made news. Suspense
before revelation: ask the room to commit (write down a prediction, a number,
a choice) and only then show the answer.

Text on slides is a reminder for the lecturer, not the script. If a slide has
more than ~40 words, cut. Prefer a figure that carries the point; decoration is
fine sometimes, but most figures should do the storytelling. Figures are
generated in R in the deck so they render anywhere; portraits and photos are
linked from Wikimedia Commons.

Pauses go at the joints of an argument, not on a clock, and each one asks for
something with a right answer or a commitment in it (PEDAGOGY.md, punctuated
lectures). Retrieval of earlier weeks is spread through the lecture where the
old idea is used, not bunched at the end.

Timing lives in the speaker notes of the first slide (total 85 inside the
90-minute booking; segments with their tier, core / compress / optional; the
standing five-minute set; the cut order naming where each cut's teaching
function lands; three or four pace waypoints), never on a slide. The notes are
stripped from the public render; they are still not the place for anything a
student must not see, because the instructor render keeps them. No "learning
outcomes" or "what is examinable" slides. No week numbers in slide bodies or
the footer (name the mechanism, not the calendar). No citations of our own
material.

Every [board] item: one slide with a recall *question* (asked at the point of
need; a box that would print the answer the board script is written to elicit
becomes the question, a box that only fixes notation stays, labelled as
notation) and the statement to leave, then backup derivation slides with
class="backup" and visibility="uncounted". Figures drawn from simulated data
say so on the slide or in the caption.

Slide attributes used by the theme:
  {.inverse}                          section divider (dark)
  {.backup visibility="uncounted"}    backup derivation slide
  [board]{.board}                     badge marking the move to the board
  ::: {.recall}                       notation box (a genuine key, not a pre-empted answer)
  ::: {.leave}                        the statement to leave on the board
  ::: {.ask}                          a question the room answers (commit first)
  ::: {.notes}                        speaker notes
-->
